A.the threefold people, Δωριέες, so called from their three tribes (᾽Υλλῆς, Δυμᾶνες, Πάμφυλοι), Od. 19.177 ; “πάντες δὲ τριχάϊκες καλέονται τρισσὴν οὕνεκα γαῖαν ἑκὰς πάτρης ἐδάσαντο”
Hes. Fr. 191
. ( Apollon. ap. Sch. Od. l. c. compares κορυθάϊξ-ῑκος and explains it as 'shaking the hair of their crests'; others rendered it τρίλοφοι, and others ὀρχησταί: more prob. Hesiod is right as to the sense; the first part is τρίχα (Adv.), the second not ἑκάς (as Hes. seems to suggest) but ϝῐκ- = Skt. viś- 'village', cogn. with ϝοῖκος; or ϝεικ-, another grade of the same root.)
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
